The evidence of I.O., Post-Mortem Report, FSL report and the evidence of doctor (PW-6) has proved that kerosene oil was found on the body of deceased and second, one bottle of kerosene oil was also lying in the room.

The evidence of four prosecution witnesses clearly proved that the appellant was addicted to consuming liquor – He used to demand money from the deceased and her parents quite often and also at times used to ill-treat and assault the deceased – The re was no reason to discard the evidence of the parents of the deceased who were the most natural and material witnesses to speak on such issues

aggravating_circumstances.value: Demand of dowry, ill-treatment, assault, addiction to liquor, presence of kerosene oil bottle, burn injuries on upper body

quotes.text: The incident of ill-treatment and demand of money did not occur once but on many a times and it started soon after the marriage which continued till deceased’s death. There is no reason to discard the evidence of the father and mother of the deceased who are the most natural and material witnesses to speak on such issues.
Trial court held that prosecution was not able to prove the charge of demand of dowry against the appellant and also that the deceased suffered homicidal death and ordered his acquittal
High Court reversed the order of acquittal and convicted the appellant under ss.498A and 302

Dismissing the appeal, the Court HELD: 1. A perusal of the evidence of the four prosecution witnesses clearly proved that firstly the appellant was addicted to consuming liquor, Secondly, he used to demand money from the deceased and her parents quite often; and thirdly, he also at times used to ill-treat and assault the deceased.
The evidence of four prosecution witnesses fully proved the case of the prosecution – Interference with the order of conviction not called for – Crime against women.
The High Court, accordingly, sentenced the appellant to undergo life imprisonment.

neutral_facts.value: The accused, a newlywed husband, was addicted to alcohol and frequently demanded money from his wife and her parents. He also subjected his wife to physical abuse and harassment. The wife eventually suffered severe burn injuries and died as a result. The prosecution presented evidence indicating that the accused poured kerosene oil on his wife and set her on fire. The incident occurred in the house where only the accused and the deceased were present. The deceased's body showed signs of burn injuries on the upper part, and kerosene oil was found on her body. A kerosene oil bottle was also found in the room. The deceased's family and relatives testified about the accused's behavior and the circumstances leading to her death. The prosecution argued that the accused's actions were intentional and not accidental.

The evidence of four prosecution witnesses clearly proved that the appellant was addicted to liquor, frequently demanded money from the deceased and her parents, and ill-treated and assaulted the deceased. The deceased's death was homicidal, not accidental, and the appellant was the only person present at the time of the incident.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the evidence clearly proved the appellant's guilt under Sections 498-A and 302 IPC beyond reasonable doubt. The court found that the deceased's death was homicidal and that the appellant was solely responsible for her death.

quotes.text: In the absence of any plausible explanation given by the appellant and the one which was suggested but not having been proved and further keeping in view the circumstances, the manner in which the incident occurred and material seized from the room i.e. kerosene oil bottle, it is proved beyond reasonable doubt that the appellant was responsible for causing death of the deceased.
